newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos orders three officials to look into the reported abduction of seven Palawan fishermen by Malaysian Navy officials in the nearby Barque island in Malaysia. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Seven armed men posing as policemen kidnap the acting branch manager of Phlippine Airlines in the southern Cotabato city (ALL PAPERS)

- The Central Bank says it will expand its investigation into the financially troubled Monte de Piedad & Savings Bank to include bishops as well as former bank officials now working in other banks. (MANILA TIMES)
- Former President Diosdado Macapagal is buried in the Heroes Cemetery, as the present leaders are reminded of the honesty that characterised his service to the public. (ALL PAPERS)

- The House ways and means committee is planning to drop all amendments to the corporate tax structure to be able to pass the individual income tax reform component before May 1, committee chairman Exequiel Javier says. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Allied Banking Corp, a bank majority owned by tobacco and liquor tycoon Lucio Tan, is reported to be interested in Monte de Piedad & Savings Bank. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- Mabuhay Holdngs Corp says it is keen on buying out the remaining shareholders of Westin Philippine Plaza. Mabuhay currently owns 51 percent of the hotel. (TODAY)
